reason: The cited evidence confirms that Cr coatings suffer from peeling/cracking in high-temperature steam (E2) and mentions Cr/CrN as a composite coating strategy (E1), but provides no specific data on CrN as a diffusion barrier, its in-situ formation, or its performance under the stated conditions. The key mechanistic and performance premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Cr coatings on Zr-alloys fail under high-temperature steam due to Cr–Zr interdiffusion
CrN is thermodynamically stable and acts as a diffusion barrier
An ultra-thin CrN layer at the Cr/Zr interface can be formed in-situ by reactive nitrogen incorporation
CrN barrier will reduce interdiffusion and improve oxidation resistance in both PWR and accident conditions
Cr/CrN composite coatings are a recognized ATF cladding strategy
